title: Ensure Password Policy Enforces Length and Rotation
description: A strong password policy helps protect Oracle Fusion and EPM SaaS environments against unauthorized access by enforcing minimum standards for password length, rotation, and reuse prevention for both user and administrative accounts. Enforcing password length and rotation reduces the likelihood that weak or compromised passwords are exploited to gain unauthorized access. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure Password Policy Enforces Length and Rotation

audit.command: For pre-upgrade environments: 1. Sign in as a Security Administrator or IT Security Manager. 2. Navigate to Tools, Security Console, Administration, Password Policy. 3. Verify that: Minimum length is ≥ 14 characters. Password expiration is ≤ 365 days. Password reuse prevention is ≥ 5 previous passwords. Account lockout triggers after ≤ 5 failed login attempts. For EPM and post-upgrade environments (OCI IAM Identity Domain): 1. In the OCI Console, go to Identity & Security, Domains, Security, Password Policy. 2. Confirm the equivalent settings: Minimum length ≥ 14.

remediation.command: Pre-upgrade (Security Console): 1. Navigate to Navigator Tools, Security Console, Administration, Password Policy. 2. Configure the following values: Minimum Length: 14 Require Numbers: No Require Special Characters: No Password Expiration (Days): 365 Prevent Reuse of Last Passwords: 5 Failed Sign-In Attempts Before Lockout: 5 3. Save and communicate changes to all users. EPM & Post-upgrade (OCI IAM Identity Domain): 1. In the OCI Console, open the Identity Domain Security, Password Policy. 2. Configure equivalent parameters for length, complexity, expiration, reuse prevention, and lockout. 3. Save policy updates; they take immediate effect for all users.

title: Ensure MFA is Enforced for All SaaS Users
description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires users to present an additional verification factor beyond username and password. In Oracle Fusion environments, native MFA enforcement via Identity Domain sign-on policies functions only after the environment's identity service is upgraded to OCI IAM. MFA protects against credential theft and password reuse attacks. Enforcing MFA across all SaaS users - whether they authenticate through the Fusion Identity Domain, an external OCI IAM domain, or another IdP-provides ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure MFA is Enforced for All SaaS Users

audit.command: 1. Check if the Fusion environment is upgraded to OCI IAM or uses an external IdP. 2. If on OCI IAM, review Security Console, User Categories, Two-Factor Authentication and confirm all user categories have MFA enabled. 3. If identity upgrade is not yet performed, verify that MFA is enforced via the external IdP for all users. 4. Test login with a standard SaaS user account and confirm MFA is required (native or via IdP).

remediation.command: 1. If the Fusion environment is upgraded to OCI IAM: In Fusion Security Console User Categories, Two-Factor Authentication, enable MFA for all categories. 2. If the environment is not upgraded or uses a federated IdP: Enable MFA in the external IdP or external OCI IAM domain and ensure it applies to all users accessing Fusion. 3. Communicate enrollment instructions and verify MFA enrollment via Fusion My Profile, Manage Secure Verification. 4. Perform test logins to confirm MFA prompts are consistently applied.

title: Ensure Phishing-Resistant MFA Is Enforced for SaaS Administrators and Privileged Accounts
description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires users to present an additional verification factor beyond username and password. In Oracle Fusion environments, native MFA enforcement via Identity Domain sign-on policies functions only after the environment's identity service is upgraded to OCI IAM or an external IdP. Privileged accounts are high-value targets. Enforcing MFA with phishing resistant factors reduces the risk of unauthorized administrative access even if credentials are compromised. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure Phishing-Resistant MFA Is Enforced for SaaS Administrators and Privileged Accounts

audit.command: 1. Determine if the Fusion environment has been upgraded to use OCI IAM (check Fusion environment's maintenance/upgrade status) or is using an external IdP for MFA. 2. Access the Security Console User Categories Two-Factor Authentication and confirm SaaS administrators/privileged categories have MFA enabled. Only enable factors that are considered phishing resistant. 3. If identity upgrade has not occurred, verify that MFA is enforced via the external IdP for privileged accounts. 4. Test login with a privileged account and confirm MFA prompt is required (native or via IdP).

remediation.command: 1. If identity upgrade is not finalized implement MFA via the external IdP. 2. After the upgrade, in the Security Console open User Categories Two-Factor Authentication and enable MFA for administrator/privileged categories. 3. Define valid phishing resistant MFA factors (mobile authenticator, FIDO, etc.). 4. Save settings and ensure SaaS users enroll in MFA during their next login. 5. Test that privileged accounts require MFA (OCI IAM) and fallback to IdP enrollment where needed.

title: Ensure Fusion Applications Administrators Have Access Only to Fusion Applications Resources
description: Ensure that Fusion Applications Administrators are granted Console access only to Fusion Applications resources. Their IAM policies must be scoped exclusively to the fusion-applications-family resource type, without granting access to other OCI services. Fusion Applications Administrators are responsible for managing SaaS environments, not the broader OCI infrastructure. Granting them access to additional OCI services (for example, Compute, Networking, Object Storage) ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure Fusion Applications Administrators Have Access Only to Fusion Applications Resources

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Identity & Security Policies. 2. Review policies attached to groups containing Fusion Applications Administrators. 3. Confirm that: Policies use the fusion-applications-family resource type. No broad tenancy-wide permissions (such as manage all-resources or unrelated service resource types) are present. 4. Verify that Console access for Fusion Administrators shows only Fusion Applications in the navigation menu.

remediation.command: 1. Identify the group(s) used for Fusion Applications Administrators (e.g., FusionAdmins). 2. Remove any existing policies that provide access to non-Fusion OCI services. 3. Create or update the policy to restrict privileges to Fusion Applications only: For administrators: Allow group FusionAdmins to manage fusion-applications-family in tenancy For read-only roles (if needed): Allow group FusionViewers to read fusion-applications-family in tenancy

title: Ensure Privileged and Administrative Roles Are Restricted to Known IP Addresses
description: When Location-Based Access Control (LBAC) is enabled in Oracle Fusion Applications, administrative and privileged roles must not be configured for unrestricted access. In the Fusion Security Console, privileged roles such as IT Security Manager and Application Implementation Consultant include the option "Enable Role ... Restricting administrative and privileged access to known IP ranges prevents unauthorized or high-risk logins from untrusted networks. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Ensure Privileged and Administrative Roles Are Restricted to Known IP Addresses

audit.command: 1. Confirm that LBAC is enabled for the Fusion environment. 2. Sign in to Fusion Security Console with appropriate privileges. 3. Navigate to Roles, Search, IT Security Manager (and other privileged roles). 4. Open the role and go to the Administration tab. 5. Verify that the checkbox Enable Role for Access from All IP Addresses is not selected. 6. Confirm that privileged roles are associated with the intended network perimeter or known IP range within LBAC configuration.

remediation.command: 1. Sign in to Fusion Security Console with an administrative account. 2. Navigate to Roles, Search, IT Security Manager (or equivalent privileged roles). 3. Go to the Administration tab and ensure the checkbox Enable Role for Access from All IP Addresses is cleared. 4. Verify that the role is correctly assigned to the appropriate network perimeter under LBAC settings, restricting access to known IP ranges. 5. Test access from a trusted IP and confirm the role remains functional; test from an unapproved IP to confirm access is denied.

title: Ensure Privileged Access is Certified Periodically
description: The purpose of this recommendation is to ensure that only authorized users retain elevated access, by reviewing users' abilities periodically - monthly for IT administrators and quarterly for others. Users could accumulate roles and data access as their responsibilities change, giving them elevated or unintended abilities that they could use erroneously or maliciously with substantial impact on operations and ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure Privileged Access is Certified Periodically

audit.command: Review users' abilities Manual method: 1. Navigate to Tools Scheduled Processes 2. Review User and Role Access Audit Report and User Role Membership Report (or schedule them, then review them). Automated method: 1. Initiate one or more Access Certification campaigns in Fusion Cloud Applications Risk Management using the instructions in Digitize Access Certification Workflows. 2.

remediation.command: When a role should be removed from a user either: Remove unwanted role. Leave role and monitor the transactions performed by the user (see below). 1. Review the user's actions since the previous review: Manual method: 1. Navigate to Tools Reports and Analytics. 2. Select the appropriate dashboards or reports. 3. Review the transactions that the role allows. Automated method: 1.Create Transaction Controls in Fusion Cloud Applications Risk Management that continuously monitor those transactions and initiate investigation workflows when unwanted activity occurs. 1. Deploy the appropriate controls using the instructions in Continuously Monitor Transactions.

title: Ensure Oracle Break Glass for Fusion Cloud Service Is Enabled
description: Oracle Break Glass for Fusion Cloud Service provides a customer-controlled workflow that governs Oracle personnel's emergency access to the Fusion Cloud database and middleware tiers. When enabled, Oracle cannot access customer data without explicit approval from your designated administrators for each one-off service ... Activating and monitoring the Break Glass service ensures that privileged Oracle support access occurs only under strict governance, audit logging, and time-bound approvals, reducing insider and third-party access risk. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Ensure Oracle Break Glass for Fusion Cloud Service Is Enabled

audit.command: In console: 1. Go to: Access Oracle Cloud Console 2. Select My Services → Subscriptions → Fusion Cloud Service 3. Verify that Break Glass status is Enabled 4. Verify that designated approvers are defined in the workflow 5. Verify that post-access revocation and audit logs are retained

remediation.command: In console: 1. Activate Break Glass service via Oracle Cloud Subscription management. 2. Define approvers (Fusion Cloud Administrators). 3. Enable notifications for Break Glass request/approval activities. 4. Enable post-access revocation and audit logs are retained

title: Ensure Basic Authentication Is Blocked for SOAP and REST API Integrations
description: Organizations must block the use of Basic Authentication for all SOAP and REST API integrations with Oracle SaaS Applications. This can be achieved by disabling Basic Authentication at the Fusion Applications layer and enforcing OAuth 2.0 as the only supported authentication method. Blocking Basic Authentication prevents insecure clients from connecting, even if misconfigured. Combined with monitoring, this ensures that only OAuth tokens are accepted, reducing exposure to replay attacks, credential ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.9 Ensure Basic Authentication Is Blocked for SOAP and REST API Integrations

audit.command: 1. Review your Service Request history with Oracle to confirm a request has been submitted to disable Basic Auth for APIs. 2. Confirm Oracle's response/documentation showing that Basic Auth is disabled in the environment. 3. Attempt API calls using Basic Authentication and verify they fail. 4. Use supported authentication (JWT, SAML, OAuth) to confirm the API works with secure methods.

remediation.command: 1. Submit a Service Request to Oracle SaaS Operations asking to disable Basic Authentication for APIs in your Fusion instance. 2. Include details of your current integrations (endpoints, methods) that rely on Basic Auth. 3. Confirm with Oracle that Basic Auth has been disabled in your environment. 4. Update all integrations to use supported methods (JWT, OAuth, SAML) per Oracle guidance. 5. Test all APIs to validate they function correctly under the new authentication method.

title: Ensure Integration Account Secrets Are Rotated on a Regular Schedule
description: Oracle SaaS environments often integrate with external systems using service accounts, OAuth clients, JWT signing keys, and X.509 certificates. These credentials are typically long-lived and, if not rotated regularly, may be compromised or reused by unauthorized parties. Long-lived credentials represent a significant risk if stolen, exposed in logs, or left unmanaged. Regular rotation reduces the risk window for credential misuse and aligns with best practices for key management. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.11 Ensure Integration Account Secrets Are Rotated on a Regular Schedule

audit.command: 1. Review integration accounts in Oracle Fusion Applications and identify all OAuth clients, JWT keys, and certificates in use. 2. Confirm that each credential has a documented rotation policy, including expiration and renewal dates. 3. Validate logs or change records to confirm that credentials have been rotated within the organization's defined schedule (for example, within the past 180 days). 4. Check for expired or inactive credentials and confirm they are removed from production environments.

remediation.command: 1. Develop an inventory of all integration account secrets, including OAuth credentials, JWT keys, and certificates. 2. Define a rotation schedule (for example, 90 or 180 days) aligned with organizational policy and compliance requirements. 3. Rotate each credential according to the schedule, updating dependent integrations and notifying stakeholders. 4. Remove or revoke any unused or expired credentials to reduce the attack surface. 5. Document the process and maintain records of all credential rotations for audit purposes.

title: Ensure EPM Automate Credentials Are Protected via Secure Storage
description: EPM Automate requires credentials to execute commands such as data load, snapshot management, or audit log export. These credentials must never be stored in plaintext within scripts or configuration files. Storing credentials in plaintext exposes privileged accounts to theft and misuse. EPM Automate is commonly executed with Service Administrator-level rights, making it a high-value target. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.12 Ensure EPM Automate Credentials Are Protected via Secure Storage

audit.command: 1. Review all automation scripts, scheduled jobs, and CI/CD processes invoking EPM Automate. 2. Verify that credentials are not stored in cleartext (e.g. in batch files, shell scripts, or parameters). 3. Confirm that either: The Oracle encrypted password file is being used, or Credentials are retrieved securely from an OS-level key store (e.g. Windows Credential Manager, Linux keyring) or an enterprise vault (e.g. CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault, OCI Vault). 4. Validate that credential rotation is in place and documented.

remediation.command: Use the EPM Automate encrypt command to generate an encrypted password file and update scripts to reference it instead of plaintext arguments. Alternatively, configure integration with an enterprise password vault or OS secure key store to inject credentials at runtime. Regularly rotate credentials and regenerate encrypted storage files. Audit existing automation jobs to ensure compliance and remove any residual plaintext credentials.

title: Ensure BPM Approval Rule and Workflow Configuration Changes Are Audited
description: Enable and monitor auditing for changes to BPM (Business Process Management) approval rules and SOA workflow configurations within Oracle Fusion Applications. These rules determine the routing and approval hierarchy for critical business transactions (e.g., expense approvals, journal entries, purchase orders, HR ... Approval rules define key authorization paths that enforce financial and operational controls. Unauthorized or untracked changes can enable fraudulent approvals, insider threats, or policy violations. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure BPM Approval Rule and Workflow Configuration Changes Are Audited

audit.command: 1. Access Setup and Maintenance → Manage Audit Policies → Audit Configuration. 2. Confirm that Audit for SOA/BPM Changes is Enabled (refer to Doc ID 2053746.1). Review Fusion Applications SOA Audit (Doc ID 2053746.1) 3. Verify that audit data is available through Audit Report / REST API. 4. Check for regular export or forwarding of BPM audit logs to the central logging system (OCI Logging / SIEM) for retention and correlation. 5. Review samples of recent approval rule modifications and confirm they match authorized change requests.

remediation.command: 1. Enable auditing for SOA/BPM components in Fusion's audit configuration as per Doc ID 2053746.1. 2. Ensure all BPM rule changes are routed through change management or governance workflow. 3. Configure scheduled extraction of BPM audit logs for integration with centralized audit monitoring (OCI Logging, SIEM, or Analytics). 4. Implement periodic review (monthly/quarterly) of approval rule changes by business process owners and security administrators. 5. Set up alerts or dashboards for critical workflow-change events.

title: Ensure Transactions Created/Updated by Fusion Administrators Are Monitored
description: The purpose of this recommendation is to ensure that creation, update and approval of transactions by administrators are monitored. Erroneous or malicious transactions could have substantial impact on operations, finances and legal/regulatory compliance. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure Transactions Created/Updated by Fusion Administrators Are Monitored

audit.command: Manual method: Review the transactions: 1. Navigate to Tools, Reports and Analytics. 2. Select the appropriate dashboards or reports. Automated method: Create Transaction Controls in Fusion Cloud Applications Risk Management that continuously monitor those transactions and initiate investigation workflows when unwanted activity occurs: 1. Deploy the following controls using the instructions in Continuously Monitor Transactions: 41001: Approved Payable Invoices by IT Superusers, 41002: Created or Updated Payable Invoices by IT Superusers, 41003: Created or Updated Payments by IT ...

remediation.command: 1. Reverse the transaction if possible. 2. Identify the configurations that allowed the transaction and alter them if possible -for details see the preceding recommendations.

title: Ensure Assignments of Substantial Access to EPM Administrators Are Monitored
description: The purpose of this recommendation is to ensure that pervasive or substantial abilities to view sensitive data are monitored - for example, data about accounts and financial data. Those abilities give users freedom to view sensitive data without the usual oversight. Erroneous or malicious actions could have substantial impact on operations, finances, and legal/regulatory compliance. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure Assignments of Substantial Access to EPM Administrators Are Monitored

audit.command: Identify users who have been assigned privileges that let them view sensitive data. Manual method: In EPM, identify roles that contain privileges that let users view sensitive data. Then inspect each role's user assignments. Automated method: Create Access Controls in Fusion Cloud Applications Risk Management that continuously monitor the roles' assignments and initiate investigation workflows when those assignments change. 1.

remediation.command: When a user is assigned to one of the privileges: Remove unwanted assignments. Ensure that the user complies with all data handling policies.

title: Ensure OCI Console Access Is Restricted to Administrative Accounts
description: Ensure that only designated administrative accounts are allowed to log in to the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Console. All non-admin user accounts must have the console password capability disabled, and sign-on policies must restrict Console application access to administrative groups only. The OCI Console provides broad administrative access. Restricting console login exclusively to administrative accounts minimizes the risk of unauthorized changes and reduces the attack surface in case of credential ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure OCI Console Access Is Restricted to Administrative Accounts

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Identity & Security Domains Users. For each non-admin user, confirm that Can use Console password is unchecked under Edit User Capabilities. 2. Navigate to Domains Security Sign-On Policies. Verify there is a policy rule that allows Console access only for designated administrative groups. Confirm that a deny rule is in place for all other users.

remediation.command: 1. For each non-admin user: Navigate to Identity & Security Domains Edit User Capabilities. Uncheck Can use Console password. Save changes. 2. Update the Sign-On Policy for the identity domain: Add a rule that allows Console login only for users in an Admin group. Add a default deny rule for all other users. 3. Test the configuration by attempting Console login with both an admin and a non-admin account.

title: Ensure All API Based Integrations Use OAuth Authentication
description: All API based integrations with Oracle SaaS Applications must use OAuth 2.0 authentication configured through the Fusion Identity Domain. Basic Authentication, long-lived static passwords, or legacy authentication mechanisms must not be used for API or integration access. Basic Authentication and static credentials present significant risks, including credential theft, replay attacks, and the inability to enforce least-privilege access. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.10 Ensure All API Based Integrations Use OAuth Authentication

audit.command: 1. Review all configured SOAP and REST integrations in Fusion Applications and Oracle Integration Cloud. 2. Confirm that integration clients are registered as OAuth clients in the Fusion Identity Domain and that Basic Authentication credentials are not in use. 3. Examine Fusion audit logs to identify API requests authenticated with Basic Authentication. 4. Review OCI IAM Identity Domain authentication logs to confirm that API access tokens are issued via OAuth flows only. 5. Validate that no unscoped or legacy credentials are present in active integrations.

remediation.command: 1. Identify integrations currently using Basic Authentication by reviewing Fusion audit logs and OCI IAM authentication records. 2. Register OAuth clients in the Fusion Identity Domain for each integration, assigning only the required scopes and authorized resources. 3. Reconfigure integrations to use OAuth tokens in place of Basic Authentication credentials. 4. Disable or revoke Basic Authentication credentials in Fusion Applications and IAM domains. 5. Establish a recurring process to review Fusion and IAM logs to detect any attempted Basic Authentication use.

title: Ensure Dormant Accounts and Orphaned Identities Are Automatically Detected and Disabled
description: Dormant accounts and orphaned identities should be detected and disabled using automated identity governance capabilities. Policies should be configured in OCI Identity Domains or integrated identity governance platforms to automatically flag and disable accounts that have not logged in within a defined period, or ... Automated detection and disabling reduces reliance on manual reviews, minimizes human error, and ensures consistent enforcement. This strengthens the organization's security posture and reduces the window of opportunity ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.13 Ensure Dormant Accounts and Orphaned Identities Are Automatically Detected and Disabled

audit.command: 1. Verify that identity governance policies are configured to automatically detect dormant and orphaned accounts. 2. Review policy logs to confirm detection and disabling actions have occurred. 3. Check for exceptions or exclusions and validate that they are documented and approved.

remediation.command: 1. Implement identity governance tooling in OCI Identity Domains or an integrated IAM solution. 2. Configure policies to flag accounts inactive for more than 90 days or lacking ownership/role assignments. 3. Set policies to disable such accounts automatically while notifying administrators. 4. Define exceptions for service accounts and apply compensating monitoring controls. 5. Periodically review policy effectiveness and adjust thresholds as needed.

title: Ensure Network Perimeters are Configured in IAM or the Identity Provider
description: Network Perimeters restrict where users can sign in to Oracle SaaS applications by enforcing trusted IP ranges or network sources. For upgraded environments, this is configured natively in Oracle Identity Domains. Restricting access to approved IPs or network locations at the identity layer reduces the risk of compromised credentials being used from untrusted or malicious networks. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure Network Perimeters are Configured in IAM or the Identity Provider

audit.command: 1. For upgraded environments: Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Console. Navigate to Identity & Security, Domains, Security, Network Perimeters. Verify that at least one Network Perimeter is defined with authorized IP ranges and attached to sign-on policies. 2. For non-upgraded environments: Review conditional access or equivalent policies in the IdP. Confirm that rules are applied to restrict authentication attempts to approved IP ranges or network locations.

remediation.command: 1. Upgraded environments (OCI IAM): Go to Identity & Security, Domains, Security, Network Perimeters. Create a perimeter with approved IP ranges. Attach the perimeter to sign-on policies. 2. Non-upgraded environments (external IdP): Configure conditional access rules in the IdP (Azure AD, Okta, etc.). Define approved IP ranges or geolocation-based conditions. Apply these rules to authentication policies used by Oracle SaaS.

title: Ensure OCI Console Access Is Restricted to Trusted Networks
description: Ensure that access to the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Console is restricted to trusted networks (secure VPNs or private network endpoints) by configuring IAM Network Sources The OCI Console provides administrative access. If user credentials are compromised, unrestricted access from any IP address increases the attack surface. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure OCI Console Access Is Restricted to Trusted Networks

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Identity & Security, Domains, Security, Sign-On Policies. Confirm that console login rules reference a defined network source (for example, request.networkSource.name = <TrustedSource>). Verify that there is no policy rule permitting console access from any network. 2. Navigate to Identity & Security, Network Sources. Confirm that the trusted network source contains only approved IP addresses, CIDR blocks, or VCN subnets.

remediation.command: 1. Define a Network Source with trusted IP ranges or VCN subnets: Navigate to Identity & Security, Network Sources, Create Network Source. Add approved IPs or CIDRs. 2. Update the Sign-On Policy for the identity domain: Add a rule that allows console login only if request.networkSource.name matches the trusted network source. Add a default deny rule for all other networks. 3. Test access from both inside and outside the trusted network. 4. Maintain a secure break-glass account exempt from the restriction.

title: Ensure Access to Fusion is restricted via Access Control List (ACL)
description: An Access Control List (ACL) restricts connections to Oracle Fusion SaaS environments by allowing access only from defined public IP addresses, CIDR ranges, or Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Virtual Cloud Networks (VCNs). Enabling ACLs enforces strict network perimeter controls around Oracle Fusion environments. By limiting access to trusted IPs or VCNs, ACLs protect against unauthorized access attempts from the public internet and ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure Access to Fusion is restricted via Access Control List (ACL)

audit.command: 1. Sign in to the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Console with the appropriate administrator privileges 2. Navigate to the Fusion SaaS environment's network settings and locate the Access Control List configuration 3. Verify that ACLs are enabled for the environment 4. Confirm that the ACL contains only trusted public IP addresses, CIDR ranges, or OCI Virtual Cloud Networks (VCNs) 5. Check that the allowlist excludes overly broad ranges such as 0.0.0.0/0 6.

remediation.command: 1. In the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Console, access the Fusion SaaS environment's network configuration 2. Enable the Access Control List feature if not already active 3. Add the organization's trusted public IP addresses, CIDR ranges, and/or OCI Virtual Cloud Networks (VCNs) to the ACL 4. Save the configuration and confirm that the ACL is enforced 5. Remove any broad or unnecessary ranges that could allow access from untrusted sources 6. Document any exceptions that must remain open, including justification and approval 7. Validate the changes by testing access from both allowed and disallowed networks to ensure enforcement is functioning as expected

title: Ensure Location-Based Access Control (LBAC) is enabled
description: Location-Based Access Control (LBAC) restricts user access to Oracle Fusion SaaS products based on network location. It applies to both user interface (UI) and API sign-ins. Access is allowed only from registered IP ranges, such as corporate offices or VPN gateways. Enabling LBAC enforces a perimeter-based restriction on where users and integrations can connect from. This complements authentication and role-based authorization by ensuring that even valid credentials cannot be used ... Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure Location-Based Access Control (LBAC) is enabled

audit.command: 1. Confirm that the IT Security Manager role is assigned 2. In a test or non-production environment, validate LBAC configuration before enabling in production 3. Navigate to Navigator, Tools, Security Console, Location Based Access 4. Verify that Enable Location Based Access is selected 5. Review the IP Address Allowlist to ensure it contains valid IPv4 or CIDR ranges for trusted networks 6. Confirm that the IT Security Manager role is designated as public to preserve administrative access 7.

remediation.command: 1. Use an account with the IT Security Manager role to configure LBAC 2. In the Security Console, open the Location Based Access tab and select Enable Location Based Access 3. Add trusted IP addresses or CIDR ranges, including the administrator's current IP to avoid lockout 4. Save the configuration and confirm the change 5. Mark the IT Security Manager role as public to preserve console access even from unregistered networks 6. If disabling LBAC, deselect the option; allowlist entries remain stored for reuse 7. Validate by testing login from both trusted and untrusted IPs

title: Ensure Geolocation Filtering with WAF for SaaS is enforced
description: Geolocation filtering in WAF for Oracle Fusion Applications restricts access based on the source country or region of incoming requests. WAF policies can be configured to allow or block traffic from selected geographies, helping organizations limit access to regions where legitimate users are located. Restricting access to only the countries or regions where the organization operates reduces unnecessary exposure to malicious traffic. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Ensure Geolocation Filtering with WAF for SaaS is enforced

title: Ensure Shared EPM Accounts Are Monitored
description: The purpose of this recommendation is to ensure that sharing of EPM user accounts is monitored. Sharing of accounts could have substantial impact on operations, finances and legal/regulatory compliance. For example, sharing makes it impossible to identify the person who performed an erroneous or malicious action. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.6 Ensure Shared EPM Accounts Are Monitored

audit.command: Identify accounts that are used by more than one person. Manual method: In EPM, identify accounts. Automated method: Create Transaction Controls in Fusion Cloud Applications Risk Management that continuously monitor account use and initiate investigation workflows when those assignments change. 1. For example, deploy the following controls using the instructions in Continuously Monitor Transactions: 45001: Shared User Accounts in EPM Account Reconciliation and 45002: Shared User Accounts in EPM Financial Consolidation and Close.

remediation.command: When an account is shared: 1. Either: o Inactivate the account. o Change the account password and share the new password with only one user. o Allow sharing to continue and monitor the transactions performed by the users (see below). 2. Review actions since the account was shared.

title: Ensure Dormant Accounts and Orphaned Identities Are Reviewed and Disabled
description: Dormant accounts and orphaned identities should be identified and disabled on a regular schedule. Dormant accounts are active accounts that have not been used for a defined period, such as 90 days. Orphaned identities are accounts with no associated owner or role assignment. Inactive or orphaned accounts present unnecessary risk, as they may still be accessible but not actively monitored. Regular reviews reduce the chance that attackers exploit forgotten accounts to gain unauthorized access. Reported as a manual review item: these Fusion/EPM/OCI IAM settings are reviewed in the Oracle SaaS and OCI consoles or reports.
reference: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.14 Ensure Dormant Accounts and Orphaned Identities Are Reviewed and Disabled

audit.command: 1. Generate user activity reports for Fusion Applications or OCI Identity Domains. 2. Identify accounts with no sign-in activity for at least 90 days. 3. Identify accounts without assigned roles, groups, or owners. 4. Confirm that such accounts are reviewed and, if appropriate, disabled or removed.

remediation.command: 1. Establish a policy defining thresholds for dormant accounts (for example, 90 days inactivity). 2. Schedule quarterly reports of user activity and ownership. 3. Review results with application owners. 4. Disable or delete dormant and orphaned accounts once confirmed unnecessary. 5. Document results and keep evidence for audit purposes.
